body:
먼저 밝히면 제가 만든 앱입니다. 문제가 되면 지우겠습니다.

하루에 같은 말을 몇 번 치는지 세어 본 적이 있는데, 계좌번호, 집 주소, "회의 중이라 이따 연락드릴게요" 같은 게 생각보다 많더라고요. 한 번은 계좌번호를 한 자리 틀리게 보낼 뻔해서, 그 뒤로 이런 걸 키보드에 넣어 두는 앱을 만들어 쓰고 있습니다.

제가 실제로 쓰는 것들
계좌번호, 주소, 사업자번호: 키보드에서 탭 한 번
견적 안내: "{이름}님, 견적 {금액}원입니다" 처럼 빈칸만 골라서
여권번호: Face ID로 잠가 두고 필요할 때만
복사한 것: 키보드 '최근' 칸에 남아 있어서 아까 복사한 걸 다시 찾기 쉬움

요즘은 키보드 자체로 글도 칠 수 있게 돼서(23개 언어) 기본 키보드와 오갈 일이 줄었습니다. 쓰던 키보드가 편하면 단축어만 넣고 원래 키보드로 돌아가게 둘 수도 있어요.

단축어를 100번 넣을 때까지 모든 기능이 무료이고, 그 뒤엔 한 번 결제나 연 구독 중 고르면 됩니다. 단축어 내용은 기기와 본인 iCloud에만 저장돼요.

https://apps.apple.com/kr/app/id1543660502

불편한 점이나 있었으면 하는 기능 말씀 주시면 바로 반영해 보겠습니다.
bodyEn:
Full disclosure: I made this app. Happy to take this down if it breaks the rules.

I once counted how many times a day I type the same things: my account number, my address, "In a meeting, will call you back." It was a lot. After nearly sending an account number with one wrong digit, I built a keyboard that keeps these for me.

What I actually use it for
Account number, address, business ID: one tap on the keyboard
Quotes: "Hi {name}, the quote is {amount}" with only the blanks to pick
Passport number: locked behind Face ID
Copied text: it stays in the keyboard's Recent tab, so I can find what I copied earlier

It now types too (23 languages), so I switch keyboards less. If you prefer your own keyboard, it can switch back after inserting.

Every feature is free for your first 100 inserts, then a one-time purchase or yearly subscription. Snippets stay on your device and your own iCloud.

https://apps.apple.com/app/id1543660502

title: [iOS] 클립키보드 – 계좌번호·주소·답장을 키보드에서 탭 한 번
angle: 루리웹 앱 홍보 게시판은 공식 홍보가 허용된다. 기능을 짧게, 그림 2장 붙여서
body:
안녕하세요, 혼자 iOS 앱을 만드는 개발자입니다.

클립키보드는 자주 치는 글을 키보드에 넣어 두는 앱이에요.

단축어: 계좌번호, 주소, 자기소개를 탭 한 번에
템플릿: 이름·날짜 같은 바뀌는 자리만 골라서
스택: 여러 값을 차례로
스마트 클립보드: 복사한 것이 종류별로 정리
문자 인식: 카드·서류 찍고 필요한 부분만 손가락으로 훑기
23개 언어 자판: 키보드를 바꾸지 않고 치면서 바로 넣기

단축어를 100번 넣을 때까지 모든 기능이 무료입니다. Pro는 한 번 결제 또는 연 구독이에요.

https://apps.apple.com/kr/app/id1543660502

(그림: 키보드에서 단축어 넣는 장면, 템플릿 빈칸 고르는 장면)
bodyEn:
Hi, I'm a solo iOS developer.

ClipKeyboard keeps the text you type often inside your keyboard.

Snippets: account numbers, addresses, intros in one tap
Templates: pick only the parts that change, like names and dates
Stacks: several values in order
Smart clipboard: what you copy, sorted by type
Text recognition: photograph a card or document and swipe the part you need
23-language keyboard: type and insert without switching

Every feature is free for your first 100 inserts. Pro is a one-time purchase or a yearly subscription.

https://apps.apple.com/app/id1543660502

(Images: inserting a snippet from the keyboard, picking template blanks)

title: 같은 말을 다시 칠 때의 작은 긴장
angle: 2026-10-25 @lee25_ios 에 올림. 앱 미리보기 영상(docs/screenshots/preview/ko/app-preview.mp4)과 스크린샷 01-reply · 03-template-fill 을 함께.
body:
계좌번호를 보내다 한 자리 틀린 걸 전송 직전에 본 적이 있어요.

그때 알았는데, 같은 말을 다시 칠 때마다 저는 아주 조금씩 긴장하고 있었더라고요. 틀리면 어쩌지 하는 그 작은 긴장이요. 시간보다 그게 더 피곤했던 것 같아요.

그 뒤로 자주 치는 말들을 키보드에 넣어 두는 앱을 만들어서 쓰고 있어요. 쓰고 나서 제일 크게 달라진 건, 보내기 전에 숫자를 한 번 더 들여다보는 버릇이 없어졌다는 거예요.

혹시 하루 동안 같은 말을 다시 칠 때마다 한 번씩 세어 보신 적 있으세요? 해 보면 어떤 말이 제일 많이 나올지 궁금해요.
bodyEn:
I once caught a wrong digit in my account number right before sending it.

That's when I noticed I was a little tense every time I retyped the same things. That small "what if it's wrong" tension. It tired me more than the time it took.

Since then I've been using an app I made that keeps the things I type often on my keyboard. The biggest change is that I no longer stare at the numbers one more time before sending.

Have you ever counted, for one day, every time you retype the same thing? I'm curious what would come up most.

title: The 5 things I stopped retyping on my phone (and how)
angle: 자기홍보 규칙이 빡빡하다. 방법이 먼저고 앱은 끝에 한 줄, 내 앱이라고 밝힌다. 할인 얘기 금지, 링크 넣지 않는다(물으면 댓글로). 같은 글을 24시간 안에 두 곳에 올리지 않는다. 첫 두 시간은 댓글에 답한다. 리뷰 부탁 · 업보트 부탁 · 제목 이모지 금지.
bodyEn:
I counted how often I type the same things on my phone. It was a lot. Here is how I cut it down. My own app shows up at the end, but the first fixes need nothing extra.

1. Email and address: Settings > General > Keyboard > Text Replacement. A short abbreviation expands into the full text. Free and built in.
2. Account number: you can put it in Text Replacement too, but I didn't like it popping up as an autocorrect suggestion, so I keep it elsewhere.
3. Stock replies: just keeping your best-written version in Notes and copying it raises the quality of every reply.
4. Replies where only the name and date change: this is where Text Replacement ran out for me.
5. The thing I copied a minute ago: iOS only remembers the last one.

For 4 and 5 I ended up building ClipKeyboard (disclosure: it's my app). It puts templates with blanks and your copy history inside the keyboard.

What do you retype the most?

title: [iOS] ClipKeyboard – a keyboard for the things you retype, now typing in 23 languages
angle: 개발자 자기 앱 글 허용, 제목에 [iOS]. 메인 피드는 리뷰 20개 이상이거나, 실명과 개인정보처리방침 · 이용약관 공개가 필요하다. 막히면 그달 'App Shelf' 메가스레드에 같은 글을 댓글로. 영상 docs/media/clipkeyboard-demo-en.mp4 (클립키보드 레포) 를 글에 직접 올린다. 같은 글을 24시간 안에 두 곳에 올리지 않는다. 첫 두 시간은 댓글에 답한다. 리뷰 부탁 · 업보트 부탁 · 제목 이모지 금지.
bodyEn:
Hi, I'm Leeo, the solo developer behind this one.

ClipKeyboard keeps the text you retype (account numbers, addresses, stock replies) inside your keyboard, so it's one tap in any app.

What it does
- Snippets: one tap, exactly as saved
- Templates: leave blanks for the parts that change, pick values when you use it
- Stacks: several values inserted in order
- Smart clipboard: what you copy is kept and sorted (emails, phones, addresses, IBANs, cards)
- Text recognition: photograph a document and swipe over just the part you need
- Secure snippets behind Face ID
- Full keyboard in 23 languages (no kanji conversion for Japanese/Chinese yet)

Price: every feature is free for your first 100 inserts. After that, what you made keeps working, and Pro is a one-time purchase or yearly.

Privacy: snippets stay on your device and your own iCloud. No third-party analytics SDK.

https://apps.apple.com/app/id1543660502

Feedback welcome, especially from people who answer customers from their phone.

title: ClipKeyboard: an iPhone keyboard that remembers your account numbers, addresses and replies
angle: 앱 쇼케이스 서브. 글 하나에 앱 하나. 짧게. 영상 docs/media/clipkeyboard-demo-en.mp4 (클립키보드 레포) 를 글에 직접 올린다. 같은 글을 24시간 안에 두 곳에 올리지 않는다. 첫 두 시간은 댓글에 답한다. 리뷰 부탁 · 업보트 부탁 · 제목 이모지 금지.
bodyEn:
What it is: an iOS keyboard that holds the text you type again and again.

Who it's for: anyone who sends the same bank details, address or replies from their phone. Freelancers and people doing customer support use it the most.

What makes it different from Text Replacement: templates with blanks you fill per message, a copy history right in the keyboard, Face ID for sensitive snippets, and it types in 23 languages so you don't have to switch keyboards.

Free for the first 100 inserts, then Pro as a one-time purchase or yearly.

https://apps.apple.com/app/id1543660502

Made by me, a solo dev. Happy to answer anything.

title: How do you handle sending the same payment details and client replies from your phone?
angle: 자기홍보 금지에 가깝다. 질문 글로 쓰고 링크 없이. 앱 이름은 본문 끝에 한 번만, 누가 물으면 댓글로 링크. 같은 글을 24시간 안에 두 곳에 올리지 않는다. 첫 두 시간은 댓글에 답한다. 리뷰 부탁 · 업보트 부탁 · 제목 이모지 금지.
bodyEn:
Genuine question, and I'll share what I do.

Between invoices, "payment received, thank you" messages and "here are my bank details" emails, I was retyping the same handful of things from my phone every week. Once I caught a wrong digit in my account number right before sending it to a client, and that was the end of typing it by hand.

What works for me now:
- Bank details, tax ID, address: saved once, inserted with one tap
- Replies where only the client name, amount or date changes: saved as a template with blanks
- Anything sensitive (passport number for contracts abroad) locked behind Face ID

I do this with a keyboard app I built myself (ClipKeyboard), so I'm biased. Not linking it since that's not what this sub is for.

How are the rest of you handling this? Text Replacement, a notes file, something else?

title: For those who message in two or more languages: how do you keep addresses and bank details at hand?
angle: 광고로 보이면 바로 지워진다. 경험 공유 + 질문, 링크 없이. 23개 언어 자판이 이 서브에 맞는 이야기. 같은 글을 24시간 안에 두 곳에 올리지 않는다. 첫 두 시간은 댓글에 답한다. 리뷰 부탁 · 업보트 부탁 · 제목 이모지 금지.
bodyEn:
Working with clients and landlords in different countries, I kept running into the same two annoyances on my phone:

1. Switching keyboards back and forth between languages several times in one conversation.
2. Retyping the same IBAN, address and "I'll be there at…" messages in each language.

What finally helped me was keeping all of it in one keyboard: it types in the languages I need, and the saved stuff (IBAN, local address, the same reply in English and Korean) sits on that same keyboard, one tap away. Full disclosure, it's an app I built myself (ClipKeyboard), so take that into account. Not linking it here.

Curious how others deal with this. Do you just live with the globe key, or have you found a better setup?

title: Goldweek: shows which days off turn a public holiday into the longest break
angle: r/iosapps 본 피드는 리뷰 20개 이상이거나 실명+개인정보처리방침+이용약관을 갖춰야 한다. 조건이 안 되면 매달 올라오는 App Shelf 메가스레드에 댓글로 이 글을 올린다. 개발자 본인임을 밝히는 줄은 지우지 말 것. 첨부(본 피드일 때): docs/screenshots/marketing/en/01-home.png, 02-recommend.png.
bodyEn:
Dev here, this is my app.

Goldweek looks at upcoming public holidays and tells you how many leave days you'd need for how many days off in a row, bridge days included. Holidays for 42 countries with regional options, custom holidays if yours isn't covered, and you choose your weekend days.

It also keeps your leave balance (half days, comp days with expiry dates), has a Home Screen widget, and backs up to iCloud. Works on iPhone and iPad.

Free to download. Paid tiers add the full-year planner and a few extras.
https://apps.apple.com/app/id6755983135

title: Did you pick up the local habit of stretching public holidays into long weekends?
angle: r/expats는 홍보 금지. 링크 없이 질문 글로만 올리고, 마지막에 본인 앱이 있다는 것만 한 번 밝힌다. 첨부 없음. 링크를 달라는 댓글이 있으면 그때 댓글로 App Store 링크를 준다.
bodyEn:
In Korea, when a public holiday lands on a Tuesday or Thursday, a lot of people take the day in between off and turn it into a four or five day break. It's a pretty normal thing to plan around.

I've been reading about how other countries handle this and it seems common in some places (Germany calls it Brückentag, France "faire le pont") and almost unheard of in others.

For people who moved countries for work:

Did you start doing it the local way, or keep your home country's habits?
Does your contract follow local holidays only, or did you negotiate something for your home holidays?
If you moved somewhere with a Friday-Saturday weekend, how long did it take before planning time off felt normal?

Full disclosure, I'm a developer and I make a small iPhone app for planning leave around holidays, which is why I'm curious how this works in practice. Not linking it here, but happy to share if anyone wants it.

title: Burning Parchment, a bedtime countdown you blow out at the end of the day
angle: r/iosapps 본 피드 조건(리뷰 20개 이상, 또는 실명+개인정보처리방침+이용약관)이 안 되면 App Shelf 메가스레드에 댓글로. 개발자 공개 줄 유지. 첨부: docs/screenshots/raw-en/blowout-dark.png, docs/screenshots/marketing-en/01-week-dark.png.
bodyEn:
I'm the developer.

It shows the time left until bedtime as parchment slowly burning, instead of a number. You can switch to the week, month or year, and add a deadline. From half an hour before bed you can blow on the screen to put the flame out (it uses breath strength only, nothing recorded), and write one line on the scrap that's left.

Home and Lock Screen widgets, plus a Live Activity that by default only shows in the hour before bed.

Free, with a one-time Pro purchase for themes and extras. No subscription.
https://apps.apple.com/app/id6758995390

title: [Question] A countdown to bedtime never worked on me. What actually got you off your phone at night?
angle: r/getdisciplined는 홍보 금지, 제목에 [Question] 같은 태그를 붙이는 관례가 있다. 링크 없이 경험+질문 글로만. 마지막 한 줄로 본인 앱만 밝히고, 요청이 있을 때만 댓글로 링크.
bodyEn:
I lose most evenings the same way. Get home, eat, sit down "for a minute", and suddenly it's past midnight. The time I had was never long, it just vanished without me noticing it go.

What I noticed is that a number like "2h 40m left" doesn't do anything to me. I read it and keep scrolling. What did seem to work a bit was seeing the time as something physically getting smaller, and having a small thing I had to do to end the day instead of just drifting into bed.

I'm curious what's worked for other people, especially anyone who managed to keep it up for more than a couple of weeks:

A hard cutoff time? Phone in another room? Some kind of end-of-day ritual?

(For transparency: I ended up building a small iPhone app around the "time shrinking" idea, so I'm biased. Not posting a link, I'm more interested in what's worked for you.)

title: Has anyone kept a one-line-a-night journal instead of a full one?
angle: r/Journaling은 앱 홍보 글을 지우는 편이다. 링크와 앱 이름 없이 한 줄 일기 방식에 대한 질문으로만. 마지막에 본인이 그런 앱을 만들었다는 것만 밝히고 링크는 요청 시에만.
bodyEn:
Full journaling never sticks for me. A page feels like homework by day three.

Lately I've been thinking about the smallest possible version: one line, written right before bed, about what the day actually went to. Not how I felt, just where the time went.

A few things I'm unsure about:

Do you sort them somehow (by theme, project, person) or just keep them in date order?
Do you ever go back and read them? If yes, how often, and does it change anything?
Is one line too little to be worth rereading a year later?

I should say I'm a developer and I built this into an app of mine, where the one-liners get grouped by topic and you can read them back like a small book. So I'm asking partly to see whether that matches how people who journal for real actually do it.

title: Kids Schedule: photograph the daycare's monthly calendar and it goes into Apple Calendar
angle: r/iosapps 본 피드 조건이 안 되면 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글로. 개발자 공개 줄 유지. App Store ID는 레포에서 확인 못 함(기존 초안 값), 링크 확인 필요. 1.0.5 출시 전이면 영어 화면 문장 삭제. 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/01-scan.png, 04-reminders.png.
bodyEn:
I'm the developer of this one.

Take a photo of the monthly schedule from daycare or preschool, check what it read, and it adds the whole month to a calendar for your child. Text recognition happens on the device. You can also paste a message from the teachers and it pulls out dates and things to bring.

Reminders the evening before or that morning include your packing note. Share the schedule with your partner or grandparents by link, works with more than one child, and there's a Home Screen widget.

Free, no in-app purchases. It was built around Korean daycare notices first, so English ones may still trip it up.
https://apps.apple.com/app/id6789881830

title: How do you keep track of the daycare's monthly calendar?
angle: r/Parenting은 홍보에 엄격하다. 링크 없이 질문 글로만, 마지막에 앱을 만들었다는 것만 밝힌다. 'Daycare' 류 플레어가 있으면 고른다. 링크는 요청이 있을 때만 댓글로.
bodyEn:
Ours sends home a paper calendar at the start of every month. Picnic on the 9th, bring a lunchbox. Gym clothes on Tuesdays. Pajama day. Parent observation day. Then extra reminders come by text in between.

For a while I typed everything into my phone calendar by hand. It took a while every month and we still missed things, usually the ones that need you to pack something the night before.

How do other families handle it? Fridge and hope? One parent owns it? Shared calendar? And do your partner or the grandparents actually look at it, or does it end up being one person's job anyway?

Disclosure since it's relevant: I'm a developer and I ended up making a little app that reads a photo of the calendar into the phone's calendar. Not linking it, I'm more curious whether other people even find this a problem or if it's just us.

title: Foreign parents with kids at a Korean 어린이집: how do you handle the monthly notices?
angle: r/korea는 자기 홍보를 지운다. 링크 없이 질문 글로만, 끝에 한국인 개발자이고 앱을 만들었다는 것만 밝힌다. 이 앱이 한국 어린이집 양식에 맞춰져 있어 이 독자층이 가장 잘 맞는다. 1.0.5(영어 화면)가 나간 뒤에 올릴 것.
bodyEn:
Korean parent here. Our daycare sends a monthly schedule sheet plus a stream of notices through the app or by text: what to pack, theme days, outings, which days the bus runs differently. Even reading it in my own language I miss things.

I've been wondering how this goes for parents who don't read Korean comfortably. Do you translate every notice with Papago, rely on a Korean-speaking partner, or ask the teachers directly? Are there daycares that send things in English?

Mostly asking because I made a small iPhone app that turns a photo of these schedules into calendar events, and I recently added an English interface. I'd like to know if it would actually help foreign parents or if the real pain is somewhere else. Not linking it, but happy to if anyone asks.

title: Toesagak, a FIRE tracker that keeps everything on your phone
angle: r/iosapps 본 피드 조건이 안 되면 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글로. 개발자 공개 줄 유지. App Store ID는 레포 미확인(기존 초안 값). 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en/01-dashboard.png, 02-assets.png.
bodyEn:
Developer here.

Log your assets by type (property, stocks, funds, pension, cash, deposits, crypto, loans) and it shows progress toward your FI number and a projected date. Market prices can refresh stock and crypto values, and a weekly record is saved automatically so you get a history chart. There's a demo profile if you just want to look around.

No account, nothing leaves the device unless you export a backup file. Free, with a one-time Pro purchase for extra calculators and a few other tools.
https://apps.apple.com/app/id6779654854

title: How often do you actually update your net worth tracking?
angle: r/Fire는 홍보 글을 지운다. 링크·앱 이름 없이 추적 습관에 대한 질문으로만. 끝에 앱을 만들었다는 것만 밝히고, 요청이 있으면 댓글로 링크.
bodyEn:
I tracked mine in a spreadsheet for years, one tab per asset type, and I'd update it in bursts. Three weekends in a row, then nothing for two months, then a painful catch-up.

Two questions for people who've stuck with it:

How often do you update, and was that a deliberate choice? Monthly seems to be the default advice, but weekly felt more motivating to me even though it's noisier.

Do you separate money you could actually live on from money that's locked up (pension, a house deposit, a mortgage)? Mine all went into one total for a long time and it made the FI number look closer than it was.

Disclosure: I eventually turned my sheet into an iPhone app, so I've obviously got opinions about this. Not here to link it, I'd rather hear how other people's systems work.

title: Rainbow Craft, a week planner that subtracts your fixed routines first
angle: r/macapps는 개발자 글에 본인 개발임을 밝히고 가격 정보를 쓰도록 한다(플레어도 개발자용으로). 링크 허용. 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/01-week.png, 02-drag.png, 03-timeline.png. 지난 9월 오퍼코드 글을 이미 올렸다면 같은 서브에 너무 가깝게 다시 올리지 말 것.
bodyEn:
I'm the developer.

Rainbow Craft is a time blocking app for the week. You lay down sleep, meals, work and other fixed routines first, and it shows how many of the week's 168 hours are actually left. Then you drag to-dos onto days and they turn into blocks.

What it does:
- Week grid and a 24-hour day timeline that shows gaps and overlaps
- Brings in events from Calendar on your Mac, and can write plans to its own separate calendar if you want them on your phone
- Breaks big tasks into steps and marks which ones fit into a spare five minutes
- Timer that follows your plan, plus a Now Timer widget
- Weekly review, one card per day

Mac only (macOS 14+), with to-dos syncing over iCloud to the iPhone app Rainbow of Desire. No account, no developer server, and analytics are anonymous counts you can turn off.

Pricing: free to download. Pro is $2.99/month, $14.99/year or $39.99 once, for longer-range stuff like trends and reusing past weeks.
https://apps.apple.com/app/id6777737322

title: Do you subtract your fixed hours before planning the week?
angle: r/productivity는 자기 홍보를 제한한다. 링크·앱 이름 없이 토론 글로만. 끝에 Mac 앱을 만들었다는 것만 한 줄 밝히고, 요청 시 댓글로 링크.
bodyEn:
Something I only did recently: before writing a single task for the week, I blocked out everything that isn't negotiable. Sleep, meals, commute, work hours, the gym.

Out of 168 hours I had about 46 left. I'd been planning as if I had double that, which explains a lot of Wednesdays.

Curious if others do this, and where you draw the line. Do chores count as fixed? Time with family? Do you leave a buffer, or does everything left over go to tasks?

(I build a Mac planner that works this way, so this is partly me checking whether the idea holds up outside my own head. Won't link it unless someone asks.)

title: StaffSinger - hear a few bars of sheet music played back in time
angle: 리뷰 0개라 메인 피드 조건(리뷰 20개 이상, 또는 실명+개인정보처리방침+이용약관)을 못 채운다. 이달의 App Shelf 메가스레드에 댓글로 단다. 개발자 고지는 첫 줄에 이미 들어 있다. 링크 허용. 이미지는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en/01-piano.png.
bodyEn:
Dev here, this is my own app.

StaffSinger is for the moment you hit a passage you can't sight-read. Copy those bars onto the staff and it plays them back with the right rhythm and pitch, with a count-in and metronome, highlighting the note that's sounding.

Covers whole notes to sixteenths, dots, triplets, rests, chords, multiple voices, key signatures, and treble, alto and bass clefs. You can also say do re mi on the beat to enter notes, or paste a score written as text. You can keep a photo of your score on screen while you copy.

Free, no IAP, no account. iPhone and iPad, landscape.
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6779262832

title: How do you learn the rhythm of a tricky passage before the next rehearsal?
angle: 자기 홍보에 엄격한 커뮤니티라 링크를 넣지 않는다. 진짜 질문으로 올리고, 마지막에 내 앱이라는 사실만 한 번 밝힌다. 이미지는 붙이지 않는다. 링크 요청이 오면 댓글로만 준다.
bodyEn:
Question for the section singers here.

When a new piece comes in and there's a bar or two where the rhythm just won't sit, usually a dotted figure running into a triplet, what do you actually do before the next rehearsal?

The options I know of are clapping it against a metronome, waiting for a learning track if your director makes them, or leaning on the person next to you and hoping. None of them feel great when it's only two bars and you need it by Thursday.

I'm asking partly because I built a small iPhone app for this (you copy the bars in and it plays them back in time), and I want to know whether that matches how singers really practise or whether I'm solving the wrong problem. I won't link it here, but I'm happy to share if anyone's curious.

title: If you don't play piano, how do you check the notes of your part?
angle: 보컬 테크닉 중심 커뮤니티다. 홍보 글로 보이면 지워지니 링크 없이 질문만 올리고, 앱 이야기는 끝에 한 문장. r/choir 글과 최소 일주일 띄운다.
bodyEn:
Genuine question. Plenty of singers read a bit but don't play an instrument, and the usual advice is "plunk it out on a keyboard."

For people in that spot: what do you actually use? A keyboard app? A tuner? Recordings? Someone else in your section?

What I'd like to know is where it breaks down for you. Finding the starting pitch, holding your line against a chord, or getting the rhythm right?

Disclosure: I made an iPhone app that plays back notes you copy onto a staff, so I have an obvious interest. Not posting a link, just trying to understand the problem better.

title: Punching - press and hold the camera to make a moving sticker
angle: 리뷰 0개라 이달의 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글로 단다. 개발자 고지 필수(첫 줄). 링크 허용. 이미지는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en/06-camera.png.
bodyEn:
I'm the developer.

Punching is a camera with a hole-punch window in the middle. Press and hold, and it keeps the short motion around your press as a moving sticker. With a clear subject it cuts that out. Without one, it punches a stamp with perforated edges.

Stickers go straight into the Messages sticker drawer and a keyboard for other apps, and they stay animated when sent. You can also turn old photos into stickers, pick a look like sepia or faded, and print a sticker book on sticker paper.

Free, no IAP, everything stored on device.
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6779659029

title: For people who print their own photo stickers, what paper and printer setup actually works?
angle: 취미 커뮤니티라 홍보로 보이면 안 된다. 링크와 이미지 없이 인쇄 용지에 관한 진짜 질문으로 올리고, 내 앱이라는 점은 끝에 한 번만 밝힌다. 답이 오면 앱의 PDF 인쇄 기능 개선에 참고한다.
bodyEn:
I've been working on something that lays out photo stickers on a printable sheet with stamp-shaped cut lines, and it made me realise I know very little about the printing side.

If you print your own stickers for pages:

Matte or glossy sticker paper? Does one hold up better once it's on a page?
Home inkjet, or do you send it out?
Do you cut by hand from printed lines, or does everyone here have a cutting machine by now?

Mostly I'd like to know what goes wrong. Colours coming out dull, edges peeling, ink smearing, that kind of thing.

For transparency, the thing I'm working on is my own iPhone app. I won't post it here, but I can share if someone wants it.

title: Rainbow of Desire - a week grid that darkens as your work piles up
angle: 리뷰 0개라 기본은 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글. 이 앱은 개인정보처리방침과 이용약관(Apple 표준 EULA)이 있으니 실명으로 올릴 생각이면 메인 피드도 가능하다(사이드바 최신 규칙 먼저 확인). 개발자 고지와 유료 요소를 밝힌다. 이미지는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en/02-list.png.
bodyEn:
Developer disclosure: I made this.

Rainbow of Desire shows your weeks as a grid that gets darker where tasks overlap, so you can spot a heavy week early. You split big tasks into steps, and it marks which steps fit into a five-minute gap and which need a real block of time. Swipe a row to bolt it to the top when it's ready to do right now. There's a timer that counts down to when the current event ends, with Live Activity support.

Free core with no account. Widgets, calendar import, sharing and stats are Pro (yearly with a free first week, monthly, or lifetime). There's a separate Mac app that syncs over iCloud.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6755280882

title: Do you sort tasks by whether they fit a five-minute gap?
angle: 자기 홍보 금지 규칙이 엄격하다. 링크·이미지 없이 개념 질문으로 올리고, 내 앱 이야기는 마지막 한 문장으로만. 댓글에서 링크를 물으면 그때만 준다.
bodyEn:
Something I keep noticing: twelve five-minute gaps in a day are not an hour. They don't add up, mostly because each one starts with "wait, where was I."

The filter I've settled on for broken-down tasks is two questions. Can I start this cold, without reloading context? And will it be fully done in five minutes, with nothing left hanging? Only steps that pass both go on the "grab it in a gap" pile. Everything else gets protected time.

Do any of you split tasks this way, or something similar? Curious whether the "start cold" part matters as much for other people as it does for me.

(I ended up building this into an iPhone app of my own, so I'm biased. Not linking it here.)

title: KORA - Korea subway guide that tells you which side to board
angle: 리뷰 0개라 이달의 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글로 단다. 개발자 고지와 유료 요소를 첫머리에 밝힌다. 링크 허용. 이미지는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/01-route.png.
bodyEn:
Developer here, my own app.

KORA is a subway app for visitors to Korea. Pick start and destination and it shows transfers, stops, time, and the train to board written the way the destination sign shows it. A camera check tells you if you're on the right platform side. While riding it tracks your station and vibrates before your stop, with a Live Activity.

Seoul area, Busan, Daegu, Gwangju, Daejeon. 23 languages. Route search works offline.

Free for routing, arrivals and the camera check. Ride alerts are free for three trips, then a one-time Pro purchase. No subscription or ads.
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6775176578

title: Where did the subway actually trip you up on your trip?
angle: 여행자 커뮤니티라 홍보 글은 지워질 수 있다. 링크 없이 경험을 묻는 글로 올리고, 앱 이야기는 끝에 한 번만. 답에서 나온 역 이름과 상황은 앱 개선 메모로 남긴다.
bodyEn:
For anyone who's used the Seoul or Busan subway as a visitor: what was the moment you got confused?

My hunch is it's rarely the map itself. It's more like standing on a platform not sure which side is yours, a transfer corridor that goes on forever, or realising one stop too late that you've passed yours.

I'd love to hear specific stations if you remember them. Big transfer stations, airport line connections, anything.

Full disclosure, I'm a developer here and I make a subway app for visitors, so this is partly research. I'm not posting it, but happy to share it if someone asks.

title: How do you explain Line 9 express vs local to friends visiting Seoul?
angle: 현지 커뮤니티. 링크와 이미지 없이 질문으로만 올린다. r/koreatravel 글과 최소 일주일 간격. 앱 언급은 마지막 한 문장.
bodyEn:
Line 9 has express and local trains on the same platform, and it's easy for a visitor to get on the first one that comes and watch it sail past their stop.

When friends visit, how do you explain it? Just "wait for the right colour on the sign"? Tell them to stay on locals? Something else?

I'm asking because I added an alert for exactly this to a subway app I make for visitors (it warns you if an express is going to skip your stop) and I want to know if there's a simpler rule people already use that I should be pointing them to instead.

title: LectureQ - catch questions during lectures with one shortcut [free]
angle: 개발자 본인 글임을 반드시 밝히고(첫 줄), 사이드바의 자기 홍보·플레어 규칙을 먼저 확인한다. 링크 허용. 이미지는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en/02_capture.png 와 01_main.png.
bodyEn:
I'm the developer.

LectureQ is a native Mac notebook built around the questions you have while watching a lecture, course or webinar.

Command Shift N from the app, or from Shortcuts and Spotlight, captures a question with the current time. Questions sit beside the time-block notes they came from, follow-ups nest underneath, and you can filter to unresolved ones. When you want answers, it copies a ready-made prompt with your notes from that moment to the clipboard for whatever AI chat you use. The app makes no network calls.

Also: lecture summary, question graph, timeline overview, Markdown import of conversation transcripts, adjustable text size.

Free, no account, data stays on your Mac. macOS 14+.
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6794597095

What would make you actually keep it open during a lecture?

title: What do you do with the questions you have in the middle of a lecture?
angle: 공부 커뮤니티라 홍보를 막는다. 링크·이미지 없이 질문으로 올리고, 내 앱이라는 사실은 마지막에 한 번만 밝힌다. 링크 요청이 오면 댓글로만.
bodyEn:
Mid-lecture, something doesn't click. You can't interrupt (or it's a recording), so you think "I'll look it up after."

Then after comes and it's gone. Or you remember the question but not the part of the lecture it was about.

How do you handle that? Margin notes with a timestamp? A separate list? Just ask right away?

My guess is the timestamp matters more than the wording, since going back to that moment tends to bring the question back. I ended up making a small Mac app around this idea, so I'm biased. I won't link it, but I'm genuinely curious what's working for other people.

title: Does anyone else keep forgetting which Sunday E-mart is closed?
angle: 자기 홍보 제한이 있는 생활 정보 서브. 링크 없이 질문 위주로 쓰고 마지막에 한 번만 본인 앱이라고 밝힌다. 첨부 없음. 게시 전에 사이드바 규칙에서 홍보 금지 조항을 한 번 확인할 것.
bodyEn:
Genuine question for people living here. How do you keep track of the mart closing days?

It's twice a month, but which days depends on the district. A lot of places do the 2nd and 4th Sunday, others do Wednesdays, and Costco branches don't all follow the same rule. I've walked to a closed store with a shopping list more times than I'd like to admit.

Do you just check Naver before going, or is there a trick I'm missing?

Full disclosure, I got annoyed enough that I made a small free app for this, so take that into account. Not linking it here, but happy to share if anyone wants it. Mostly curious how others deal with it.

title: PSA-ish: mart closing days aren't the same everywhere, and Costco branches differ too
angle: r/korea 는 홍보성 글에 엄격하다. 생활 정보 글로 쓰고 링크는 넣지 않으며, 앱 언급은 마지막 한 줄. 반응이 있어도 댓글로 링크를 먼저 뿌리지 말고 요청이 있을 때만.
bodyEn:
Something that tripped me up for a long time, in case it helps anyone newer here.

Large supermarkets have mandatory closing days twice a month, but which days depends on your local government. Many areas use the 2nd and 4th Sunday. Some switched to Wednesdays. A few regions such as Ulsan and Jeju have their own pattern. Costco branches are not all the same either, so the one in Daegu or Ilsan can differ from the one you usually go to. Seollal and Chuseok add extra closed days.

Smaller restaurants are their own thing again, with fixed weekly days off that are usually only listed on Naver Map.

Is there a source people here trust for this? The store websites are hit or miss.

(I ended up writing a small free iPhone app for myself to track it. It's my own app, I'm not posting a link, but can share if someone asks.)

title: DontGoMart - know whether your Korean supermarket is open today
angle: 짧은 쇼케이스용. 링크 허용. 두세 문단으로 끝낸다. 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en/03-marts.png 또는 01-main.png.
bodyEn:
Small iPhone app for people in Korea. Big supermarkets and Costco close on mandated days that vary by region, and it's easy to forget which.

Pick your stores and the app shows if they're open today, counts down to the next closing day and reminds you ahead of time. You can also add restaurants' regular days off by pasting a Naver Map link or a screenshot. Widgets for home and lock screen. Free.

https://apps.apple.com/app/id6450387984

title: Do you plan new routes on purpose, or do you end up on the same loop every day?
angle: 걷기 커뮤니티. 홍보 링크 없이 경험·질문 글로, 앱은 마지막에 한 번만 밝힌다. 이미지는 올리지 않는 편이 자연스럽다.
bodyEn:
Something I noticed after I started keeping a map of only the places I had actually walked, starting from a blank page: the empty patches were right next to home. Streets ten minutes away that I had simply never had a reason to take.

Walking the same route again doesn't add anything to that kind of map, so it nudges you toward the unfamiliar street instead of the usual loop. I didn't expect that to change how I walk, but it did.

Curious how others here think about it. Do you deliberately pick new streets, or is the familiar loop the whole point for you?

(The blank map is a free iPhone app I made, so I'm biased. No link here, happy to share if anyone asks.)

title: [Dev] Buktu Buktu, a blank map that only fills in where you walk (free)
angle: 개발자 본인 표시 필수. 리뷰 20개 미만이면 메인 피드가 아니라 월간 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글로 올린다. App Store ID 를 레포에서 확인하지 못했으므로 링크는 확인 후 추가. 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/02-compass.png.
bodyEn:
I'm the developer.

Buktu Buktu is a map that starts blank. Only the places you walk get filled in. Car and subway trips aren't drawn, and repeating the same route doesn't grow it.

You can stamp places you've been or want to go (212 stamps), photograph a shop sign to turn it into a cut-out sticker on the map, see each day's walk drawn as a shape in a calendar, and export a short film of your map being drawn over a period you pick. Home and lock screen widgets.

Free, no in-app purchases, data stays in your iCloud. 24 languages.

title: Anyone practice with a voice-controlled click? Wondering how it holds up over a kit
angle: 악기 커뮤니티는 홍보 금지가 일반적. 링크 없이 질문 글로, 본인 앱이라는 사실은 마지막 한 번만. 첨부 없음.
bodyEn:
Question for people who practice with a click a lot.

I made a metronome you control by talking to it. Say "faster" or "tempo 140" and it changes without you touching anything. Speech recognition runs on the phone, through the app's own mic. Drums are the obvious stress test, and I honestly don't know how well that copes with someone hitting a crash two feet away.

For those of you who change tempo mid-session, how do you do it now? Stop and tap the screen, a foot pedal, something else? And would talking to it even be practical, or is the volume a dealbreaker?

Disclosure: it's my own app, free for the basic metronome. Not dropping a link, but I'll share if anyone wants to try it and tell me how it does.

title: Changing metronome tempo without putting the violin down
angle: 악기 커뮤니티 질문 글. 링크 없음, 마지막에 본인 앱임을 밝히고 원하면 공유한다고만. 첨부 없음.
bodyEn:
Curious about a small practice thing. When you work a passage from slow to fast, how do you bump the metronome up without breaking position? Letting go of the instrument to tap a phone seems to cost more focus than it should.

I ended up making a metronome that takes spoken commands, so you can say "up" for one BPM or "faster" for five between repetitions. There's also a mode that adds a few BPM every few bars by itself.

It's my app, so I'm not neutral. Mainly wondering whether string players find this a real problem or already have a simpler habit that works. Happy to share it if anyone asks.

title: [Dev] Not My Tempo, a metronome you control by voice
angle: 개발자 표시 필수. 리뷰 20개 미만이면 월간 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글로. 유료 구성 그대로 표기. 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/01-playing.png.
bodyEn:
Dev here. Not My Tempo is a metronome you change by talking to it, so both hands stay on the instrument. Speech is recognized on device through the app's own mic, no iOS Voice Control setup needed.

Free: meters 1 to 8, subdivisions, tap tempo, three beat visualizers, timing check. Pro (yearly or lifetime): speed trainer, accent editor with per-song presets, chromatic tuner.

https://apps.apple.com/app/id6781537149

title: Do you fall asleep better to one sound or a mix of a few?
angle: r/sleep 는 홍보에 엄격하다. 링크·이름 없이 질문 글로 쓰고, 맨 끝에 직접 만든 앱이 있다는 것만 밝힌다. 의학적 효과 주장은 하지 않는다.
bodyEn:
I used to lose a ridiculous amount of time every night scrolling for something to fall asleep to. The right video never quite existed.

What eventually helped was building my own mix once and reusing it, instead of searching fresh every night. The other thing I learned: a sound that stops abruptly when the timer ends can wake you right back up, so a slow fade matters more than I thought.

Curious what works for others. One steady sound, a layered mix, or silence? And do you leave it on all night or use a timer?

(For transparency, I make a sleep sounds app, which is partly why I'm asking. Not linking it, but I can if someone wants.)

title: [Dev] Dalbit, layer your own sleep sounds and run it all from one moon
angle: 개발자 표시 필수. 리뷰 20개 미만이면 월간 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글. 1주 무료 체험 구독임을 숨기지 않는다. 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/02-studio.png.
bodyEn:
I'm the developer. Dalbit lets you stack sleep sounds (rain, water drops, birdsong, singing bowls and more), set each layer's volume, frequency and position, then save the mix and play it with one tap on the moon.

Sleep timer fades out instead of cutting, plays with the screen off, gentle alarm sounds for the morning. iPhone and iPad.

All sounds free, three saved mixes free. A subscription with a one-week trial unlocks unlimited mixes.

https://apps.apple.com/app/id1626715109

title: What gets you to write on the days you least want to?
angle: r/Journaling 은 앱 홍보 글을 자주 지운다. 링크 없이 경험·질문으로, 앱은 마지막에 한 번만 밝힌다. 첨부 없음.
bodyEn:
My journaling always fell apart on exactly the days it would have helped. After a bad day I'd open a blank page, look at it, and close it again.

What I eventually realized is that a blank page asks the most of you right when you have the least. Answering a small question, like "what got in the way today?", is a lot easier than starting from nothing. Saying it out loud instead of writing also lowers the bar on hard days.

I'm curious what others do. Prompts, a fixed template, just one line, or skipping and not feeling bad about it?

Full disclosure, I turned the question-first idea into a small app, so I'm not unbiased. I won't link it here, but happy to if anyone's interested.

title: [Dev] ZinggumDol, a gentle journal for setbacks
angle: 개발자 표시 필수. 리뷰 20개 미만이면 월간 App Shelf 메가스레드 댓글. 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/03-path.png (징검다리 주간 화면).
bodyEn:
Dev here. ZinggumDol is a journal for days that go wrong. A pebble asks first, remembers your last answer, and when you miss a goal it asks what got in the way. Reply by tapping, typing or speaking (on-device recognition).

Weeks are shown as stepping stones, and missed days stay visible. Home screen widget, optional daily reminder, passcode lock, no sign-up, entries in your own iCloud.

Free up to three goals; one-time Pro purchase for more. 24 languages.

https://apps.apple.com/app/id6450388408

title: SkyDex: a 48-color board you fill by photographing the sky
angle: r/iosapps 본 피드는 리뷰 20개 이상이거나 실명+개인정보처리방침+이용약관이 필요하다. 이 앱은 docs/ 에 privacy.html 은 있지만 이용약관 페이지가 없고 리뷰 수도 확인되지 않았으니, 이번 달 "App Shelf" 메가스레드에 댓글로 단다(이 title 은 메가스레드 형식에 맞춰 첫 줄로 쓴다). 개발자임을 밝히고 링크 하나만.
bodyEn:
Dev here, this one's mine.

SkyDex fills a board of 48 sky colors, from dawn to night, each time you photograph the sky. No scoring, any sky goes in. Each color gets a name, you can add a line, and spots slowly fade if you don't shoot that time of day again for a while.

iPhone, no account, Home Screen widgets.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6802295390

title: Does anyone keep a daily log that's mostly not words?
angle: r/Journaling 은 홍보 글을 지우는 편이라 링크 없이 경험·질문 글로 쓴다. 맨 끝에 한 번만 직접 만든 앱이라고 밝히고, 원하면 링크를 주겠다고만 한다. 사진 첨부 없이 글만.
bodyEn:
I take a lot of photos of the sky and almost never look at them again. Lately I've been trying something smaller instead: keep only the color of the sky at that moment, plus one line about whatever was on my mind. Not about the sky, just the thought.

My hunch is that the color might do more of the remembering than the words. A gray 4pm and a pinkish 7pm feel like completely different days even if the line is boring.

I'm curious if others do something similar. A color, a photo, a song, a single word per day? And does it hold up when you look back months later, or does it only mean something in the moment?

(Full disclosure: I ended up building a small iPhone app around the sky-color version of this for myself. Happy to share it if anyone asks, but I'm more interested in what other people's low-word journals look like.)

title: StickyPresenter - notes, timers and a teleprompter that stay above full-screen slides
angle: r/macapps 는 개발자 본인 글이면 첫 줄에 밝혀야 한다(플레어가 있으면 개발자 플레어). 링크 허용. 첨부는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/02-timers.png. 개인정보 문장은 APPSTORE.md 그대로(익명 사용 통계 있음).
bodyEn:
I'm the developer.

StickyPresenter is a menu bar app for people who present from a Mac. Notes and countdown timers float above everything, including full-screen Keynote, without taking focus away from the slides.

- Timers resize up to room-readable, and a timer can open as its own window so you can share just that window over screen sharing or AirPlay
- Teleprompter with speed control and mirror mode
- Command-Control shortcuts that work from any app

There's also a free iPhone remote for the timer. No account, notes never leave the Mac; apart from anonymous usage stats it only goes online if you send feedback. macOS 14+.

One question for people who present a lot: do you show the countdown to the audience or keep it to yourself? I added the shareable timer window mostly for workshops and I'm not sure how common that is.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6778457299

title: How do you keep track of time when your slides are full screen and the clock is gone?
angle: r/PublicSpeaking 은 홍보를 허용하지 않는다. 링크 없이 실제 고민을 묻는 글로 쓰고, 끝에 한 번만 직접 만든 Mac 앱이 있다고 밝힌다. 첨부 없음.
bodyEn:
This has happened to me more than once. I go full screen in Keynote, the menu bar clock disappears, my notes are on a laptop I can't really look at without turning away, and suddenly I have no idea whether I'm at minute 12 or minute 20.

Presenter view helps when there's a second screen, but not every room gives you one.

What do you all do? A phone timer on the lectern? A watch? Someone in the back holding up cards? I'm also curious whether people who use a countdown actually look at it, or whether it just makes them more nervous.

For context, I ended up writing a little Mac app that floats a timer and notes over full-screen slides, because I'm a developer and that's how I deal with problems. Not linking it here, but I'm happy to if anyone wants. Mostly I want to know what works for people who don't have that option.

title: Made a small Mac utility for checking app colors against Dark Mode and Increased Contrast
angle: r/macapps, 개발자임을 첫 줄에 밝힌다. 링크 허용. 일반 Mac 사용자보다 디자이너·개발자용 도구라는 걸 분명히 해서 엉뚱한 기대를 막는다. 첨부는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/03-color-vision.png.
bodyEn:
Developer of this one. It's aimed at designers and app developers rather than everyday Mac use, so skip if that's not you.

TetraTint takes a color and generates the Dark, high-contrast and dark high-contrast versions, checks a whole palette for contrast problems, and shows how the palette looks with protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia or monochromacy. It can pull in the Okabe-Ito, IBM and Paul Tol colorblind-safe palettes, and there's a screen with the system colors from Apple's guidelines in all four modes, click to copy.

It's in 24 languages now, and there's a Shortcuts action that picks a color off the screen.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6789206198

title: How do you pick Increased Contrast variants for custom colors?
angle: r/iOSProgramming 은 앱 홍보를 토요일 "App Saturday" 플레어로만 허용한다. 반드시 토요일에 그 플레어로 올리고, 개발자 대 개발자 질문 위주로 쓴다. 링크는 맨 끝에 하나. 첨부는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en-US/02-contrast.png.
bodyEn:
Posting this for App Saturday, but it's half a real question.

For custom colors in an asset catalog, I used to fill in Any and Dark and leave the High Contrast slots empty. When I finally tried to do it properly, the approach I settled on was: dark gets slightly brighter and more saturated, light high contrast gets pushed until it hits 4.5:1 on white, dark high contrast until 7:1 on black. That roughly matches how the system colors behave across modes.

I turned that into a Mac tool, TetraTint. It generates the four variants, lets you adjust them, and exports Contents.json, a .colorset, or UIKit/SwiftUI code. It also does a whole-palette audit and generates UIFontMetrics / relativeTo / @ScaledMetric code for custom fonts with Dynamic Type.

The question: does anyone do this differently? For example, do you treat high contrast as a separate design pass with a designer, or derive it mechanically like this? And has anyone actually had users mention Increased Contrast?

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6789206198

title: Is 7:1 on black a reasonable target for a dark high-contrast color, or overkill?
angle: r/accessibility 는 홍보 글을 받지 않는다. 링크 없이 기준에 대한 진짜 질문으로 쓰고, 끝에 한 번만 이 계산을 하는 도구를 직접 만들었다고 밝힌다. 첨부 없음.
bodyEn:
I build small iOS and Mac apps, and I've been trying to give my custom colors proper variants for the system's Increased Contrast setting instead of leaving them blank.

What I landed on: in light mode with increased contrast, push the color until it reaches 4.5:1 against white. In dark mode with increased contrast, 7:1 against black. The logic was that someone who turns on increased contrast in dark mode is probably asking for more than the AA minimum.

But 7:1 against black squeezes a lot of colors toward pale pastel, and some of them start to look alike. I've also been checking palettes with color blindness simulation, and a few brand colors that were fine individually turned into near-identical pairs.

For people who audit apps or rely on these settings: is 7:1 the right call there, or would AA plus clearly distinct hues serve users better? And do you see Increased Contrast actually being used much?

(I wrote a Mac tool that does these calculations for my own apps. I'll leave it out unless someone wants it; the question is the part I care about.)

title: Bookmark Shot: save lines from paper books by swiping over them
angle: 리뷰 20개·이용약관 요건을 확인할 수 없으므로(docs/ 에 terms 페이지 없음) 이번 달 "App Shelf" 메가스레드에 댓글로 단다. 개발자임을 밝히고 짧게. 링크 하나.
bodyEn:
Made this one myself.

Photograph a page from a paper book, swipe a finger over the line you want, and just that line is saved as text along with the book and page number. A cover photo adds the title and author. Daily quote widget for the Home and Lock Screen, iCloud sync, and the text recognition stays on your phone.

Free, no ads.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6792787106

title: Do you record page numbers in your commonplace book?
angle: r/commonplacebook 은 손으로 쓰는 노트 문화가 중심이고 홍보에 민감하다. 링크 없이 질문 글로 쓰고, 끝에 한 번만 직접 만든 앱이 있다고 밝힌다. 필요하면 손글씨 노트 사진 대신 글만.
bodyEn:
Small question that's been bugging me.

When a line in a book hits me, my habit has been to photograph the page. The result is a camera roll full of pages where I can't tell which book they came from, let alone which line I meant. Copying things out by hand is the obvious fix, and it's what got me reading about commonplace books.

So, for those who keep one: do you note the page number every time? Title and author only? Some kind of index at the back so you can find a passage in context later?

I'm also wondering whether a digital capture step ruins it. Saving just the line plus the page on the phone, then copying the ones that still matter into the notebook, seems practical, but half the value of a commonplace book seems to be the act of writing it out.

(The photo part is an iPhone app I made for myself. Not posting a link since that's not the point here, but I can share it if anyone's curious.)

title: Geusaie, a pasta timer that runs each pot on its own clock
angle: r/apphunt 는 짧은 쇼케이스 글이 기본이고 링크 허용. 개발자 본인임을 밝힌다. 첨부는 docs/screenshots/marketing/en/01-home.png 또는 iPad 화면 docs/screenshots/marketing/en/ipad-02-cook.png.
bodyEn:
I made this for cooking pasta and sauce at the same time without one finishing early.

It shows one task at a time in large type, keeps a separate countdown for each pot, and shifts the rest of the plan if you start late. Say "next" to move on with wet hands. Two recipes so far. iPhone and iPad, no account.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6793473149

title: How do you get the sauce and the pasta to finish at the same moment?
angle: r/Cooking 은 자기 홍보를 금지한다. 링크 없이 요리 질문으로만 쓰고, 끝에 한 번만 직접 만든 타이머 앱이 있다고 밝힌다. 첨부 없음.
bodyEn:
My recurring problem with pasta at home is timing. The noodles are ready and the sauce still needs a few more minutes, or the sauce is done and I'm standing there waiting for the water.

What seems to help is working backwards: figure out when the pasta comes out, then count back to when the sauce has to start, instead of starting both "at the beginning." Also doing the chopping while the water heats instead of before.

I'm curious how others handle this, especially with sauces that can't sit, like anything with cream or cheese. Do you hold the pasta back, keep the sauce on low, or just have it memorized for the dishes you make often?

(I'm a developer and ended up making a little timer app that does the working-backwards part. Not linking it here, but happy to if anyone asks.)

title: Aglio e olio: when do you start the garlic relative to the pasta?
angle: r/pasta 는 사진 위주 서브라 질문 글은 짧게. 링크 없이, 앱 이야기는 마지막 한 줄로만. r/Cooking 글과 최소 며칠 간격을 둔다. 첨부 없음.
bodyEn:
Garlic timing is the part of aglio e olio I second-guess. Start it too early and it's browning while the pasta still has minutes left. Too late and it gets rushed.

When do you start yours relative to dropping the pasta? Low heat from cold oil before the pasta goes in, or once the pasta is already boiling? And do you pull the pasta a minute early to finish it in the pan?

(I ended up building a cooking timer app around this exact problem, which is a little embarrassing. Can share if anyone wants.)

title: CatchSlide (App Shelf comment)
angle: 평점 0개라 본문 피드 조건(리뷰 20개 이상, 또는 실명+개인정보처리방침+약관)을 못 채운다. 이달 'App Shelf' 메가스레드에 댓글로 단다. 개발자임을 밝히고 링크 허용. 개인정보처리방침: https://m1zz.github.io/SlideSnap/en/privacy.html (약관 페이지는 레포에서 못 찾음).
bodyEn:
CatchSlide, iPhone, $2.99 (I'm the developer)

A camera just for presentation slides. It finds the slide edges as you aim and straightens the shot, groups slides you take in a row into one talk, and reads the text so you can search it later. Also works on lecture photos you already have: share them from Photos and they get straightened in order. Exports PDF handouts. No account, no sound, on-device.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6790835318

title: What do you actually do with the slide photos from seminars and conferences?
angle: 자기 홍보 금지 서브. 링크 없이 진짜 질문으로 쓰고, 끝에 한 번만 직접 만든 앱이 있다고 밝힌다. 첨부 없음.
bodyEn:
Genuine question. At conferences and department seminars I take a lot of photos of slides, mostly a figure or a citation I want to look up later. In practice I almost never find them again. They're in my camera roll somewhere between a parking sign and a lunch receipt, and I don't remember which talk they came from.

I've seen people ask speakers for the deck, use a notes app, or just take a photo of the reference and email it to themselves on the spot.

What's your system, if you have one? And do you go back to those photos at all, or is it mostly a way to feel like you captured something?

Full disclosure, I got annoyed enough by this that I made a small iPhone app for it. Not linking it here, happy to share if anyone's curious, but I'm more interested in how other people handle it.

title: Do your professors mind when people photograph the slides?
angle: 학생 커뮤니티, 홍보 글 금지. 짧은 토론 질문으로 쓰고 링크 넣지 않는다. 앱은 마지막 줄에만 언급.
bodyEn:
In most of my lectures half the room holds up a phone every time the slide changes. Some professors seem fine with it, one asked people to stop because of the shutter noise, and another just started uploading the slides so nobody had to.

Curious how it is at other schools. Is it normal where you are, or seen as a bit rude? And if you do it, do you actually use the photos later?

(I made a slide camera app with no shutter sound partly because of this, so I'm biased. No link, just wondering what people think.)

title: MyFi: Wi-Fi QR (App Shelf comment)
angle: 평점 0개라 이달 'App Shelf' 메가스레드 댓글로 단다. 개발자 표시, 링크 허용. 약관 페이지는 레포에서 찾지 못했다.
bodyEn:
MyFi: Wi-Fi QR, iPhone, free (dev here)

Point the camera at a Wi-Fi sign or receipt and it joins the network. If it misreads, you drag the recognized bits into the right field. Also makes Wi-Fi QR codes for your network or hotspot, and printable guest signs (7 themes, logo, card or A4) for cafes and rentals. Home and Lock Screen widgets for a QR you use a lot. Nothing leaves the device.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6793472383

title: What's on your Wi-Fi card, and do guests still message you for the password?
angle: 호스트 커뮤니티, 홍보 금지. 링크 없이 질문 글로 쓰고, 끝에 한 번만 직접 만든 앱을 밝힌다. 사이드바에서 벤더·홍보 규칙을 꼭 확인할 것.
bodyEn:
Hosts seem to handle Wi-Fi details in very different ways. Some tape the password inside a cabinet, some put it in the welcome book, some have a framed card with a QR code, and plenty of guests seem to message for it anyway.

For those of you with a QR card: do guests actually scan it, or do they still type the password? And does anyone print a new card every time they change the password, or just leave it?

Small disclosure since it's relevant: I make an iPhone app that prints guest Wi-Fi signs, which is why I'm curious. I won't link it unless someone asks. Mostly trying to learn what actually reduces those messages.

title: Cafe owners, did putting a Wi-Fi QR at the counter cut down on people asking for the password?
angle: 자기 홍보 금지. 짧은 질문만, 링크 없음, 앱은 마지막에 한 줄.
bodyEn:
Quick one for anyone running a cafe or a shop with customer Wi-Fi. Did a QR code by the register actually stop the "what's the Wi-Fi" question, or do people still ask because they don't trust scanning random codes?

Also wondering whether you change the password regularly and how annoying it is to redo the sign each time.

I built a small app that makes these signs, so I have a stake in the answer. Happy to share it if anyone wants, but I'm mainly after real experience.

title: Rereminder (App Shelf comment)
angle: 미국 평점 5개라 본문 피드 조건 20개에 못 미친다. 'App Shelf' 메가스레드 댓글. 개발자 표시와 가격 모델(무료, Pro 한 번 구매)을 정확히. 설치 없이 써 볼 App Clip 링크를 함께 둔다.
bodyEn:
Rereminder: Presentation Timer, iPhone + Apple Watch + Mac menu bar. Free, optional one-time Pro (I made it)

A countdown that warns you before it ends. Drag bells on the dial for as many early alerts as you want; they're free and unlimited. Sections show their own time left, Live Activity and Dynamic Island, Watch app included. Pro is one purchase that remembers your setups. No ads, no subscription.

Try it without installing (App Clip): https://m1zz.github.io/rereminder/
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/rereminder/id6752551268

title: How do you know when to start wrapping up without staring at a clock?
angle: 연습·조언 서브, 홍보 금지. 링크 없이 실제 경험과 질문으로 쓰고, 마지막에 한 번만 직접 만든 타이머 앱이 있다고 밝힌다.
bodyEn:
I used to put a timer on the lectern and check it every few minutes. Two problems: people notice when you keep looking down, and a single alarm at the end is useless because by then you've already run over.

The one time it really bit me, I thought I had five minutes left and actually had none. I had to skip my whole conclusion.

What do people here do? A friend in the front row with fingers up? A watch that buzzes? Marking a slide as the "if I'm here at minute X, cut the next section" point?

I ended up writing my own timer app that buzzes a few times before the end, so I'm not neutral on this, but I'm more interested in what works for you than in pointing anyone to it.

title: Timekeepers, what do you use besides the green, yellow and red cards?
angle: 클럽 커뮤니티, 홍보 금지. 링크 없이 질문으로 짧게. 앱은 마지막 한 줄. 스토어 키워드에 timekeeper 가 있는 만큼 대상은 맞다.
bodyEn:
For those who take the timekeeper role: do you just run the stopwatch on your phone and flip cards by eye, or does someone have a setup that buzzes you at each mark so you're not watching the screen the whole time?

Asking because I made a timer app that alerts at several points before the end, and I'm wondering if it would be any use for this or if the cards work fine as they are. Not posting a link, just curious how clubs handle it.

title: Sekki: Photo Food Diary (App Shelf comment)
angle: 평점 0개라 리뷰 조건은 안 된다. 개인정보처리방침(https://m1zz.github.io/RoutineCamera/en/privacy.html)과 약관(https://m1zz.github.io/RoutineCamera/en/terms.html)이 레포에 있으니, 스토어 개발자명이 실명이면 본문 피드도 가능하다. 확인 못 했으니 기본은 'App Shelf' 댓글.
bodyEn:
Sekki: Photo Food Diary, iPhone. Free, optional Pro subscription or lifetime (dev here)

One photo before a meal is the entry; it files itself as breakfast, lunch, dinner or snack by time. Mark meals done from a notification, widget, Siri or the Action button. One meal a day keeps the streak, and the total never goes down. On-device food recognition, friend codes to cheer each other on.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6755164924

title: Streaks that reset to zero made me quit more habits than they kept
angle: 자기계발 토론 서브, 홍보 금지. 링크 없이 경험·토론 글로 쓰고 앱은 마지막에 한 번만 밝힌다. 사이드바의 [Discussion] 등 제목 태그 규칙이 있으면 맞춘다.
bodyEn:
Something I noticed with food logging, though I think it applies to most habits.

Every app I used had a streak counter, and it worked great until the first day I missed. Then the number went from 23 to 0 and the whole thing felt pointless, so I'd stop. The streak that was supposed to keep me going was the exact thing that made me quit.

What ended up working better for me was two changes. First, lowering the bar for what counts as a day: one meal logged is a day, not three. Second, keeping a total that never goes down next to the streak, so a bad week doesn't erase the good months.

I'm curious whether others have found the same thing, or whether a hard reset is actually what motivates you. Some people seem to need the all-or-nothing version.

Disclosure: I built a food photo diary around this idea, so I've obviously thought about it a lot. Not linking it, the question is the point.

title: ClipKeyboard for Mac, a menu bar snippet panel that syncs with my iPhone keyboard app [dev]
angle: 개발자 표시와 가격 표시가 필수다($9.99 유료 다운로드, 앱 내 결제 없음, macOS 26+). 올리기 전 사이드바에서 홍보 플레어·주기 제한·AI 사용 공개 규칙을 확인할 것. 링크 허용. 첨부: docs/screenshots/marketing/en/01-panel.png, 04-clipboard.png.
bodyEn:
Developer here. $9.99 one-time, no in-app purchases, requires macOS 26.

Control-Shift-V opens a floating panel of saved snippets over the current app without taking focus. Click one or hit Command-1 to 9 and it goes to the clipboard, then you paste with Command-V as usual. Menu bar only, no Dock icon.

- Templates with { } fields; date, time, time zone and a few others fill in automatically
- Clipboard history, 100 items kept for 7 days
- Image snippets, and secure snippets that need Touch ID or your password
- iCloud sync with the iPhone version, same order on both

No account, nothing sent to me. Backups to iCloud with the last 15 versions kept, or export to a file.

It deliberately doesn't type into the app for you, it puts things on the clipboard and you paste. Would people here rather have it paste automatically, or is that something you'd turn off anyway?

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6756433372

title: How do you deal with the text you retype ten times a day?
angle: 홍보 엄격 금지 서브. 링크 없이 질문만, 앱은 마지막 한 문장으로만 밝힌다. 삭제될 위험이 가장 큰 글이니 반응을 보고 올릴지 정할 것.
bodyEn:
Mine is mostly the same few replies to people, my address, bank details for invoices, and an email sign-off I apparently can't remember to set up properly.

I've seen people use text expansion with abbreviations, a pinned note they copy from, or just their own sent mail as a search engine. Abbreviations never stuck for me because I forget them.

What do you use, and what made it actually stick?

(Full disclosure: I make a snippet app for iPhone and Mac, so I'm partly asking to learn what people need. Not linking anything.)

title: 복사는 한 칸짜리 서랍
angle: 최근 클립 칸 — 복사한 게 덮어써져 사라지는 순간에서 시작. 사진: 02-recent-clips
body:
송장번호를 복사해 두고, 주소를 하나 더 복사하는 순간 앞의 번호는 사라지죠. 그걸 알면서도 또 하고, 다시 앱을 열어 찾고, 또 복사해요.

복사는 한 칸짜리 서랍이더라고요. 새로 넣으면 앞에 있던 게 조용히 밀려나요.

그래서 제가 만들어 쓰는 클립키보드에는 복사한 걸 차례로 쌓아 두는 칸을 넣었어요. 이메일인지, 전화번호인지, 계좌번호인지도 알아서 나눠 두고요.

다들 방금 복사한 걸 덮어써서 다시 찾으러 간 적, 하루에 몇 번쯤 있으세요?

앱스토어에서 "클립키보드" 검색하면 나와요.
https://apps.apple.com/kr/app/id1543660502
bodyEn:
You copy a tracking number, then copy an address, and the number is gone. You know it'll happen, and you do it anyway. Back to the app, find it, copy it again.

The clipboard is a drawer with one slot. Put something new in, and the old thing quietly slides out.

So in ClipKeyboard, the keyboard I build and use, everything you copy stacks up in order. It also sorts them for you: email, phone number, account number.

How many times a day do you go back for something you just overwrote?

Search "ClipKeyboard" on the App Store.
https://apps.apple.com/app/id1543660502

title: 매일 아침 세 줄짜리 출근 보고
angle: 스택 — 매일 같은 양식(이름 · 부서 · 할 일)을 순서대로. 사진: marketing/ko/04-snippet-stack
body:
회사마다 하나씩은 있는 것 같아요. 매일 아침 단톡방에 올리는 출근 보고. 이름, 부서, 오늘 할 일. 세 줄인데 매일 같은 순서로 칩니다.

이상하게 그런 건 매일 해도 손에 안 붙어요. 한 줄을 빼먹거나, 어제 할 일을 그대로 보내거나요. 매일 하는 일일수록 오히려 덜 들여다보게 되나 봐요.

그래서 제가 만들어 쓰는 클립키보드에는 값을 순서대로 넣어 두는 칸이 있어요. 키보드 버튼 하나를 누를 때마다 다음 값이 차례로 들어가요. 사진이 실제 화면이에요.

매일 같은 양식으로 보내는 거, 다들 하나씩은 있으시죠? 어떤 건지 궁금해요.

앱스토어에서 "클립키보드" 검색하면 나와요.
https://apps.apple.com/kr/app/id1543660502
bodyEn:
Every team seems to have one. The morning check-in in the group chat: name, team, today's task. Three lines, typed in the same order every day.

Oddly, it never becomes automatic. You skip a line, or send yesterday's task again. Maybe the things we do daily are the ones we look at least.

So ClipKeyboard, the keyboard I build and use, has a spot where you line up values in order. Each tap on one keyboard button types the next one. The picture is the real screen.

Everyone has some form they send the same way every day, right? I'm curious what yours is.

Search "ClipKeyboard" on the App Store.
https://apps.apple.com/app/id1543660502

title: 마지막으로 쉰 게 며칠 전이었나
angle: 첫 화면의 쉬어가는 흐름 — 지난 휴가 며칠 전 · 다음 휴가 며칠 후 · 평소 주기. 사진: marketing/ko/01-home
body:
마지막으로 쉬었던 게 언제였는지 바로 대답이 안 나올 때가 있어요. 세어 보면 두 달이 넘어 있고요.

요즘 유독 지치는 건 일이 많아서라기보다, 쉬는 날 사이가 너무 벌어져서일 때가 많더라고요. 연차는 남아 있는데도요.

그래서 제가 만든 골드위크 첫 화면에는 지난 휴가가 며칠 전이었는지, 다음 휴가까지 며칠 남았는지가 나와요. 평소에 며칠에 한 번씩 쉬는지도요. 사진이 실제 화면이에요.

다들 마지막으로 쉬어 본 게 며칠 전이세요?

앱스토어에서 "골드위크" 검색하면 나와요.
https://apps.apple.com/kr/app/id6755983135
bodyEn:
Sometimes I can't say right away when I last took a break. When I count, it's been over two months.

Lately, when I feel worn out, it's less about the workload and more that the gaps between days off got too long. Even with leave still left.

So the first screen of GoldWeek, the app I made, shows how many days ago your last break was and how many days until the next one. And how often you usually take one. The picture is the real screen.

How many days has it been since your last break?

Search "GoldWeek" on the App Store.
https://apps.apple.com/app/id6755983135

body:
새 노트 버튼, 보통 오른쪽 위에 있잖아요.
한 손으로 노트 세 개만 연달아 만들어 보면 얼마나 멀리 있는지 알게 돼요.

앱 디자인 실습은 이런 걸 일부러 틀린 화면으로 먼저 만져 보게 해요. 이상하다 싶은 데가 있었는지 적어 두고, 그다음에 이유를 보는 식이에요. 마지막엔 고친 화면이랑 같은 자리에서 바꿔 가며 비교하고요.

11월 14일까지 코드 NOVE로 평생 이용권이 무료예요.
